text:
marcus: Heads up — MerchantOne asked for a tightly-scoped POC: they need a near drop-in replacement for their current vendor with minimal prompt/response drift and predictable cost delta. Can we list technical assumptions, security asks, and blockers?

anya (SE): Summary of their must-haves: 1) identical request/response envelope (headers + body) 2) deterministic output option for A/B 3) streaming behavior matched or proxied 4) clear rollback.

priya (security): They submitted the security questionnaire. Top asks: KMS integration, key control (rotate every 90d), region isolation, audit retention, and SOC2 controls. Also want confirmation that PII isn't retained in logs.

leo (eng): Our compat proxy can translate endpoint shapes, but there are two notable differences: competitor uses chunked-json streaming and a custom session cookie for KV affinities. We stream SSE by default and use header-based affinity. We can build a small re-chunker service (SSE -> chunked-json) and support cookie->header translation, but it's a 48-72h spike for a minimal PoC.

kevin (solutions): For parity validation we'll run: 1k canonical prompts from MerchantOne domain + 300 randomized edge prompts. Measure token counts, p95 latency, top-1 semantic match (embedding similarity), and error rates. Suggest test cases at temp=0 and temp=0.7.

marcus: Pricing — they want an invoice delta and a worst-case scenario if tokenizer adds tokens. Can we provide a sample 'before/after' invoice with line items?

anya (SE): I'll generate a delta simulation. Tokenization drift often causes 3-12% token increase depending on model/tokenizer mismatch. Enabling prefix caching and batching usually offsets some cost — I'll simulate both with and without caching.

priya (security): On questionnaires: provide KMS/HSM details, key rotation policy blurb, and screenshot of audit logs retention settings. Also flag that proxying traffic back to competitor could be non-starter for regulated customers — legal needs to weigh in.

leo (eng): Another engineering caveat: competitor supports per-chunk metadata for function-calling; our function-calls are emitted as a final JSON object. We can expose an emulation layer that emits intermediate function tokens, but parity won't be perfect without a small SDK shim on their side.

kevin (solutions): Regarding cache warmup: MerchantOne relies on sticky sessions for KV. Options: run Dedicated with sticky-router or document a KV-warmup plan using synthetic requests. Acceptance criteria should assert no spike in 5xx and tokenized latency increase under X% during warmup.

marcus: Can we commit to a canary rollback approach and a threshold (e.g., semantic drift > 10% or error rate increase > 0.5%) to trigger auto-fallback?

leo (eng): Yes — we can implement routing policy: primary->redwood, fallback->origin-vendor with header X-Fallback-Reason. Implementation requires legal signoff for proxied outbound traffic. Also need to ensure headers with secrets are stripped before proxied calls.

priya (security): Legal will also want a data flow diagram for any cross-vendor proxying. If customer requires no external egress, fallback must be disabled (enterprise blocker).

kevin (solutions): Proposed POC timeline: 3d shim spike (rechunker + cookie->header), then 10 business days of automated runs with daily health checks; final decision based on parity & billing delta.

deploy-bot: deploy/compat-rechunker job started by leo — build #4821 queued

anya (SE): I'll assemble: mapping spec, 1k prompt corpus, token-delta simulation, security artifacts, rollback plan, and acceptance test scripts. Will also add a short sample invoice showing worst-case token increase.

marcus: Please have a short customer-facing runbook and timeline by EOD. Flag any items that need legal signoff clearly.

leo (eng): If legal blocks proxy fallback, we'll present an alternative: longer canary with manual failover and documented warmup.

priya (security): I'll prepare screenshots for KMS settings and a paragraph on rotation and HSM options for Private deployments. Also will mark the proxying fallback as a potential compliance blocker in the questionnaire response.

kevin (solutions): I'll curate the MerchantOne corpus and post it to the drive. Also will prepare a rubric: token delta threshold <= 15%, semantic-match >= 90%, latency p95 within 20% of baseline. If policy breaches, keep canary at 1% and require manual go/no-go.

marcus: Thanks — keep replies short. If anyone needs me on the customer call tomorrow, say so.

leo (eng): I can join for the technical deep dive.

priya (security): I'll join for questionnaire/Q&A.

kevin (solutions): I'll lead acceptance test walkthrough.

marcus: Solid. Closing — I'll draft the risk register and pricing sketch.
